steps: Follower timing: Starting with the right foot in the same place, step together on 1
On 2: go forward
On 3: step in the same place
On 5: bring it back together
On 6: step back
On 7: step in place
Leader timing: Starting with the left leg in the same place. Left, right, left, right, left, right
tips: Count 1, 2, 3, leaving a pause, then 5, 6, 7, leaving another pause -- three steps and three steps
You are NOT stepping continuously -- you take 3 steps, pause, 3 steps, pause
When stepping to the music, we count 8 beats but only step on 6 out of the 8 beats
Before you even step, identify the count of the music -- listen first
Rhythm is quick-quick-slow, quick-quick-slow
Make your steps shorter as you get comfortable

steps: Stand nice and straight, face your partner, take your partner's hand
Guys step back first since guys are leading -- step back with your left foot on 1
On 1: step back with left foot
On 2: step back with the right foot
On 3: left foot in place
On 5: right foot forward
On 6: left foot forward
On 7: right foot in place
Ladies mirror: forward right, forward left, right in place, then left back, right back, left in place
tips: Most of the weight is on your toes when stepping
In salsa it is the opposite of walking -- start with your toe touching the ground, then gradually transfer weight down
Never fully put your weight on your heel
You will be spinning on the ball of your foot, so keep weight there for easy and effective spins
Step with toes first, not the heel

steps: There is an action on the 2 and the 6 as we count from 1 to 8
Men break back on the second beat with the right foot
Men break forward on the left foot on 6
Right foot breaking on 2 (back), left foot breaking forward on 6 -- this is dancing on 2
tips: Dance precisely with the correct tempo
Notice the action on beats 2 and 6 -- these are the break steps
This is known as dancing on 2
If the music speeds up, your steps speed up with it

combined_steps: Count 1: Step in place with your right foot (leader: left foot back). This is the prep step -- not a big movement, just establishing the rhythm.
Count 2: Step forward with your left foot (leader: right foot back). This is the 'break' -- the key defining beat of On2 dancing.
Count 3: Step in place with your right foot (leader: left foot in place), collecting your weight. Slight pause follows.
Count 4: HOLD -- no step. Weight settles, body prepares to reverse direction.
Count 5: Step in place with your left foot (leader: right foot forward). Begin the second half of the basic.
Count 6: Step back with your right foot (leader: left foot forward). This is the second 'break' step.
Count 7: Step in place with your left foot (leader: right foot in place), collecting your weight.
Count 8: HOLD -- no step. Weight settles, cycle repeats.
visual_cues: Your posture should be tall and straight -- shoulders down and back, no hunching
Knees should be slightly bent throughout, never locked
Weight should be on the balls of your feet (toes), never sinking into the heels
Steps should be small and compact -- no wider than shoulder width
On counts 4 and 8 (the holds), both feet should be roughly under your body, weight centered
Arms should be relaxed at your sides, elbows bent naturally like a light jog
basic_step.practice_drill: Start by counting out loud: 1-2-3-hold-5-6-7-hold, clapping on 2 and 6 to internalize the break beats. Then do 20 basics counting aloud with steps, focusing on toe-first contact. Next do 20 basics with the rhythm 'quick-quick-slow, quick-quick-slow' to feel the timing. Finally, put on a salsa song and do 2 full minutes of basics without stopping, finding the 2 in the music before you start stepping.

steps: Start in closed position just like the cross body lead
Guys: your footwork is the same as the cross body lead
The only difference: lift your arm up on 3 and turn the follower on 5, 6, 7
Leader drew a counterclockwise circle with left hand to guide the girl into the turn
Ladies: since the guy's arm is above yours, that signals the turn -- continue turning until you see him on 7
Follower footwork: turn your right, left, right step, your left, right, left to get to the inside turn and face your partner at the end
tips: Guy's footwork is identical to cross body lead -- only the arm lead changes
Leader draws a counterclockwise circle with leading (left) hand to guide the turn
In cross body lead, follower turns on 3 to face partner -- in inside turn, the arm above signals a full turn
Follower continues turning until she sees the leader on 7
Also known as a traveling left turn

steps: Start in closed position
Guys: footwork same as cross body lead -- open up on 1, 2
On 3: lift arm up and turn the follower
On 5, 6, 7: follower completes the turn
Leader demonstrates with count: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7
tips: Same footwork as cross body lead for the leader
Leader drew a counterclockwise circle with left hand, the leading hand, to guide the girl into the turn
Ladies: in the cross body lead you turn on 3 to face partner; now since the guy's arm is above yours that signals the turn
Continue turning until you see him on the 7
Also known as a traveling left turn

steps: Open on 5, 6, 7
Start the free spin on 1, 2
Turn on 3, 5, 6, 7
Recover into cross body lead
tips: Very important for followers to remember their track (slot)
As you start the turn, maintain your track/frame throughout
The free spin variation: leader releases the hand and follower spins freely
After the free spin, recover by reconnecting hands and going into cross body lead

combined_steps: Count 1: Leader steps back with left foot (same as CBL). Leader begins to open up, creating space for the follower.
Count 2: Leader steps to the side/back with right foot, continuing to clear the slot. Follower steps forward.
Count 3: Leader steps forward with left foot and LIFTS the left arm up above the follower's head, drawing a counterclockwise circle. Follower begins the turn to her left (inside).
Count 4: HOLD -- follower is mid-turn.
Count 5: Follower continues turning. Leader steps in place, maintaining the arm guide above. Follower steps as she turns (right foot).
Count 6: Follower completes the turn, stepping with left foot. Leader steps forward.
Count 7: Both collect -- follower should be facing the leader again. Return to basic position.
Count 8: HOLD -- back to neutral.
visual_cues: Leader's left arm should rise smoothly on count 3 -- not jerky, just a gentle lift above follower's head
The arm draws a small counterclockwise circle (from leader's perspective) above the follower's head
Follower should spot the leader: look at leader, turn head first, body follows, find leader again on 7
Leader's feet trace the same path as a cross body lead -- only the arm action changes
After the turn, both partners should be facing each other squarely on 7
inside_turn.practice_drill: Solo: Practice the cross body lead footwork 10 times, then add the arm lift on 3 (raise your left hand above your own head as a placeholder). For the turn itself, stand in place and practice a slow left (counterclockwise) turn: step on the ball of your foot, spot a point on the wall, turn 360 degrees and find that point again. Do 10 solo left turns, then combine with the CBL footwork for 10 reps.

steps: Start with basic backwards: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7
On 7: when you go back, go a little bit towards your right to clear out of the way for ladies
On 1: open up and face the direction the lady will travel. Spot that direction, make sure there's nothing in the way
On 2: don't turn your body yet, but point your toe in the direction you're traveling
On 3: turn back. Now you have lady on the other side
Back to basic 5, 6, 7
Ladies: traveling in a straight line. On 1, 2 go forward. Pivot on your left foot. Step your right leg back on 3. Finish basic 5, 6, 7
tips: In one song you probably do around 50 cross body leads -- it's the most fundamental connected move
This hand (lead hand) is just for decoration in closed position -- you're leading through her back using your right hand
Lead using your frame, your body, and your footwork -- no pushing or pulling involved
Keep a good frame. Don't collapse it
At the cross position, gentlemen and ladies are perpendicular (90 degrees), not parallel
Ladies travel a straight line and only turn 180 degrees -- no halfway turns
Common mistake: guys crossing themselves instead of the lady
Common mistake for girls: the crab walk (stepping sideways instead of straight)
Get out of the way soon enough so the lady doesn't have to walk around you
It's like opening a door and inviting the lady to walk through
No pushing or pulling -- you gently ask, like a gentleman

steps: The cross body lead is essentially the basic step but you're turning as you do it
Come into closed position (different from open)
Do the basic: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7
CBL: guys open up and let the girls walk through
Guys: stepping back on left, back with right, step with left, then forward right, left, right -- same footwork as basic
Girls: your basic step but you turn on the 3. Step forward 1, 2, turn on 3, then continue basic steps
tips: Cross body lead is essentially the basic step but turning
The footwork pattern for the leader is the same as the basic: back-back-place, forward-forward-place
For followers: it is really just your basic step; the only difference is you turn on the 3
The turn on 3 and the rest is just the continuation of the basic steps

combined_steps: Count 1: Leader steps back with left foot, beginning to shift slightly to the right to clear the lane. Follower steps forward with right foot.
Count 2: Leader steps back/side with right foot, now opening the body to face the direction the follower will travel. Point your toe in that direction. Follower steps forward with left foot.

Count 3: Leader steps with left foot, turning to face forward again. The lane is now clear. Follower pivots on her left foot and steps right foot back, turning 180 degrees to face the opposite direction.
Count 4: HOLD -- leader has cleared the slot, follower has completed the pivot.
Count 5: Leader steps forward with right foot. Follower steps back with left foot (now doing the second half of her basic in the new position).
Count 6: Leader steps forward with left foot, closing back to face the follower. Follower steps back with right foot.
Count 7: Leader steps in place with right foot, returning to basic position facing follower. Follower steps in place with left foot.
Count 8: HOLD -- both partners now face each other in the new orientation. Follower has crossed the leader's body line.
visual_cues: On count 1-2, the leader should visibly shift to the right, creating a clear lane on the left for the follower
At count 2, the leader's body should face the direction the follower will travel -- like opening a door
At count 3, leader and follower should be perpendicular (90 degrees) to each other, never parallel
The follower travels in a straight line -- if she's crab-walking sideways, the lead is off
Leader should NEVER cross himself -- only the follower crosses the leader's body line
After count 7, both partners should be facing each other in the mirror, in the opposite orientation from where they started
cross_body_lead.practice_drill: Leader solo drill: Do 10 basic steps, then on the next cycle, practice stepping to the right on 1 and opening your body on 2, then closing on 3. Alternate: basic, CBL footwork, basic, CBL footwork. Follower solo drill: Do basics, then on a designated cycle, step forward 1-2, pivot 180 on 3, and continue your basic in the new direction. Both: do 20 CBL footwork patterns solo with counts, then pair up and do 10 together at slow tempo before adding music.

steps: Start with basic 1, 2, 3
Guys: on the 5-6-7, start your turn: 5, 6, 7
Then 1, 2, 3 back into basic (nose = back into facing partner)
Girls turn: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 -- same exact footwork, same steps, just on different counts
Guys go under their own arm on 5, 6, 7; girls turn on 1, 2, 3 (she pivots 5, 6, 7)
Arms: palm facing up, hers resting on top of yours
When turning ladies: draw a small clockwise circle about the size of a halo above her head
When guys go under: just skim the top of your head
tips: Same exact footwork for both leader and follower -- only difference is the counts are offset
Bend your wrists like you're holding a plate when leading
When you go under, skim the top of your head -- don't duck way down
When turning the ladies, draw a SMALL circle, about the size of a halo, above her head
The circle for the follower's turn is CLOCKWISE (from leader's perspective)

steps: From basic: 1, 2, 3 and 5, 6, 7
From basic now side, basic
Right turn: Hey, two, three. Five. Base six
One, two, three, five, six, seven (with turn incorporated)

combined_steps: Count 1: Step in place with right foot (basic prep). Begin preparing for the turn -- slight body wind-up.
Count 2: Step forward with left foot, beginning the turn to the right (clockwise). Weight transfers to ball of left foot as pivot point.
Count 3: Step with right foot, completing the first half of the turn (~180 degrees). You should be facing away from your starting position.
Count 4: HOLD -- momentum carries you through the turn.
Count 5: Step in place with left foot, collecting. If turning, complete the remaining rotation to face forward again.
Count 6: Step back with right foot, returning to basic timing.
Count 7: Step in place with left foot, collecting weight.
Count 8: HOLD -- turn complete, back in basic rhythm.
visual_cues: On the prep (count 1), your body should show a slight wind-up -- shoulders angled slightly against the turn direction
During the turn, spot a point: look at it, turn your head first, let body follow, find the point again
Stay on the ball of your pivot foot throughout the turn -- heel should not touch the ground
Keep your core tight and arms close to your body during the spin for stability
After the turn, you should be facing the same direction you started, feet under your body
Leader's lead hand: bend wrist like holding a plate; draw a small clockwise halo circle above follower's head
right_turn.practice_drill: Solo right turn drill: Stand in place, step with left foot and pivot 360 degrees to the right on the ball of your foot. Do 10 turns slowly, spotting a point on the wall. Then add the timing: say '1' (prep), '2' (step and start turn), '3' (complete turn), 'hold', '5-6-7' (basic). Do 10 reps integrating the basic step before and after the turn. Finally, alternate basic-basic-turn-basic-basic-turn for 2 minutes.

steps: The open break is very similar to the basic
In the basic: guys step forward with left foot on 6, ladies step back with right foot on 6
In the open break: guys step BACK with left foot on 6 instead of forward
5, 6, 7 -- 1, 2, 3 (basic first half), then on 5, 6, 7 the open break happens
After the open break: lift arm up and let her turn on 1, 2, 3, then 5, 6, 7 back to basic
After the open break, what you did with your feet was just go back into the basic
Adding into CBL: cross 1, 2, then open break 6, 7. Since you gave her the open break, that signals a turn -- lead her into the catwalk
tips: The reason we do this is to prep the girls for their turn
You are going AWAY from her rather than towards her -- this signals that you want her to turn
It's a signal: stepping back instead of forward tells the follower a turn is coming
After the open break, your feet just go back into the basic
The open break can be added into the cross body lead to set up turns
Can combine: CBL -> open break -> turn -> back to basic

steps: First step is on the right foot -- small step forward, a preparation to go into your basic
Without that first little step, you can't go into your basic -- you need to prepare to dance on 2
That first step is your 1 (one), then actual basic is 2, 3, 6, 7
Step right foot forward on 1 (preparation), then go into basic: 2, 3 and 6, 7
Forwards 2, backwards on the right 6
tips: On 2 you need to PREPARE before starting your basic -- the first step on 1 is a preparation
It feels slower than dancing on 1 because the transition in the pause becomes transitional, but technically it is the same rhythm
The prep is super duper important -- the steps themselves are not complicated at all
When you want to finish a pattern, step forward into your basic
Whether you lead or follow, everybody learns footwork on the follower's timing (going forward) for solo work

steps: On 1: step in place with right foot -- this is the prep. Strong step to get you back if you step off time
On 2: step left foot forward (or backward for open break)
On 3: step right foot in place
On 5: left foot in place
On 6: right foot back (for open break: go backwards instead of forward)
On 7: left foot in place
Open break: instead of going forward on the second half, go backwards -- effectively a rock step without the rotation
In place 1, on 2 backwards, 2 together 3, now back to home base 5, open break 6, 7
tips: When finding the beat, use the 1 -- it's your strong step to get back if you step off time
Stay nice and compact -- don't take big steps, stay centered
Good posture: shoulders down and back, knees bent, stay on your toes
Don't put your heel down -- keep pressure on your toe for more responsiveness
Step with the toe when transferring forward, not going onto the heel when going back
The open break is effectively a rock step -- you go backward instead of forward
Keep your weight on your toes as you go backwards, not leaning back, keeping nice posture and centeredness
Nice and responsive on the toes

combined_steps: Count 1: Step in place with right foot -- this is the PREPARATION. Use this to find the beat and establish your rhythm. It's your anchor step.
Count 2: For the open break, step BACKWARD with your left foot (instead of forward as in the basic). This backward motion signals to the follower that a turn is coming.
Count 3: Step in place with right foot, collecting weight. You've created tension by moving away.
Count 4: HOLD -- the tension from the backward step preps the follower.
Count 5: Step in place with left foot, returning to home base. Begin to settle back into basic position.
Count 6: Step backward with right foot (the open break). Leader goes away from the follower instead of toward, creating the signal.
Count 7: Step in place with left foot, collecting.
Count 8: HOLD -- the follower now knows a turn is coming on the next cycle.
visual_cues: The key visual difference from a basic: on the second half (5-6-7), the leader moves BACKWARD instead of forward
Your body should be leaning slightly away from your partner on the open break -- creating visible space between you
Your arm connection should stretch slightly but not break -- the follower feels the gentle pull-away
After the open break, the leader's arm should lift to signal the coming turn
Keep your weight on your toes even when stepping backward -- do not sink into your heels
Posture stays tall throughout -- no leaning back excessively
prep_step.practice_drill: Solo drill: Do 4 basic steps counting aloud, then on the 5th cycle replace the forward step with a backward step (the open break). Feel how your body rocks back instead of forward. Do 10 reps alternating: basic-basic-open break-basic-basic-open break. With a partner: do basic-basic-open break, then on the next cycle lift your lead hand and let the follower turn. Practice the sequence: 2 basics -> open break -> inside turn -> 2 basics, repeated 10 times.

steps.position: Side by side facing the mirror. Feet shoulder-width apart, neutral stance. Weight centered, arms relaxed at sides.
steps.instruction: Start with a full 8-count basic step. Count 1-2-3 (break) 5-6-7 (break). Both leader and follower do their own basic.
steps.instructor_tip: 6 steps total. If you are stepping more, you are losing time and the count.
steps.what_to_watch: Both dancers feet are close together, compact steps. No exaggerated movement yet.

steps.position: Connected in open position — leader holds follower with left hand. Light separation, about arms length. Leader beginning to twist body right.
steps.instruction: Prep for the left turn: twist your body to the RIGHT. This is the coil. Left hand holds follower, right hand free.
steps.instructor_tip: Twist your body to the right to prepare. This unlocks you from the right twist into the left twist on count 3.
steps.what_to_watch: Leader subtle body twist to the right visible in frame. Follower maintaining her basic.

steps.position: Arms extended between dancers creating open space. Leader has stepped to the side to open the slot. Follower beginning to rotate left.
steps.instruction: Open break into the left turn. Leader opens the lane, follower begins turning LEFT on count 3. Leader keeps doing basic — your forward does not change.
steps.instructor_tip: The turn happens on count 3. Your weight shifts and you pivot, but count 7 stays in place — just shift your weight.
steps.what_to_watch: Notice the arm extension — leader creating space, not pulling. Light connection through fingertips.

steps.position: Follower has turned 90+ degrees to the left. Leader still in basic. Both dancers feet are close together for the reset.
steps.instruction: Follower completes the turn. On count 6, you should be FACING FORWARD again. Right leg goes back on 6, not forward.
steps.instructor_tip: On count 6, you should be facing forward again after the left turn.
steps.what_to_watch: Follower feet are compact after the turn — she did not drift off the line.

steps.position: Both dancers facing the mirror, side by side, doing Suzy Q footwork. Cross-step-cross pattern visible. Hips twisting for styling.
steps.instruction: Suzy Q: cross, step, cross. Keep your back foot CLOSE behind your front foot. Do not pass your front foot. Twist your hips for the visual.
steps.instructor_tip: Cross, step, cross — keep your back foot close. Twist your hips for styling.
steps.what_to_watch: Both dancers feet are tight and compact — no wide steps. Hip rotation visible.

steps.position: Walking forward across the floor. Stepping on odd numbers only — quarter beats. Compact, rhythmic steps.
steps.instruction: Quarter beats after the Suzy Q: step only on counts 1 and 3. These are the core beats. Walk forward with intention.
steps.instructor_tip: After Suzy Q, do quarter beats by stepping only on odd numbers: 1 and 3.
steps.what_to_watch: Steps are smaller and more deliberate than regular walking. Both in sync.

steps.position: KEY FRAME: Follower arm is HIGH above head in an arc — this is the left turn with full arm styling. Leader is stepping to the side. The instructor (teal shirt) is also doing the combo to the right.
steps.instruction: Left turn with arm styling: keep arm CLOSE to your right ear on 1-2-3. Then trace your body from behind your neck (5) down your body (7) to up again (1). Do this WITH INTENTION.
steps.instructor_tip: Keep it close to your ear. Trace your body. With intention, not tentatively.
steps.what_to_watch: This is the money frame — follower arm is high and controlled, not floppy. Bent at the elbow, close to the head. The hips are rotating through the turn.

steps.position: Traveling together across the floor. Connected by one hand. Leader guiding follower path. Moving diagonally across the dance floor.
steps.instruction: Cross-body movement: leader opens the lane, follower walks through. Keep connection light — guide, do not pull. Stay on the line.
steps.instructor_tip: Leaders must be assertive with direction. Use body language and touch to show where to go.
steps.what_to_watch: One-hand connection. Leader leading with body movement not just arm. Both on rhythm.

steps.position: Partner basic step. Close position, facing each other. Both hands connected. Leader looking at follower, smiling — relaxed frame.
steps.instruction: Back to partner basic step. Hands connected, frame maintained. Leader palms up, follower palms over. Two-finger Spider-Man grip. No death grip.
steps.instructor_tip: Keep your frame. Arms at shoulder width.
steps.what_to_watch: Notice the relaxed connection — no stiff arms, no white knuckles. Both on time. Compact steps.

steps.position: Continuing partner basic, cycling through the pattern. Other students visible on the floor — the whole class is now practicing.
steps.instruction: Continue the partner basic, then restart the combo: basic -> left turn -> Suzy Q -> quarter beats -> repeat.
steps.instructor_tip: Don't lose time. Use the break between each set of 3 to reset.
steps.what_to_watch: By the end of the video, the movement is more fluid and confident. The pattern is locking in.

steps.instructor_tip: twist your arm on count 2 subtly — not exaggerated. Keep a normal step forward but add hip twist on count 2

steps.position: Leader has stepped to the side, creating the lane. Left hand lifting up and out to guide follower through. Right hand centered. Follower beginning to pivot off right foot.
steps.instruction: Leader has stepped to the side, creating the lane. Left hand lifting up and out to guide follower through. Right hand centered. Follower beginning to pivot off right foot.
steps.instructor_tip: keep your right hand centered and lift your left hand up and out

steps.position: Follower crossing through the lane — pivoting off right foot, left foot swinging left. Right elbow down maintaining frame. Leader's arms compact at shoulder width around follower's head.
steps.instruction: Follower crossing through the lane — pivoting off right foot, left foot swinging left. Right elbow down maintaining frame. Leader's arms compact at shoulder width around follower's head.
steps.instructor_tip: pivot off your right foot while your left foot swings to the left. Keep your right elbow down to maintain frame

steps.position: CBL completing. Both dancers reestablishing connection. Follower has crossed through, both returning to basic step position. Arms settling back to open position frame.
steps.instruction: CBL completing. Both dancers reestablishing connection. Follower has crossed through, both returning to basic step position. Arms settling back to open position frame.
steps.instructor_tip: When turning your follow, keep your arms at shoulder width around their head. Don't use wide arms; stay compact and controlled

video_breakdown.description: BASIC STEP -> SUZY Q (linear) -> CIRCULAR SUZY Q (around the world) -> BASIC STEP -> COMBO (card out + around + anchor) -> INSIDE TURN (right turn) -> TRANSITION BACK TO BASIC -> PARTNER WORK

steps.position: Instructor in black Adidas top faces students. Upright posture, weight centered. Students observe from the sides. The woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt are visible as the primary student group. Instructor holds a conga drum — this is the pre-fog, clear-visibility phase.
steps.instruction: Instructor in black Adidas top faces students. Upright posture, weight centered. Students observe from the sides. The woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt are visible as the primary student group. Instructor holds a conga drum — this is the pre-fog, clear-visibility phase.

steps.position: Camera angle shifted — now behind the student group. Instructor visible at left demonstrating. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt attempt the basic step. Feet show small forward travel on counts 1-2. Audience lines the walls watching.
steps.instruction: Camera angle shifted — now behind the student group. Instructor visible at left demonstrating. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt attempt the basic step. Feet show small forward travel on counts 1-2. Audience lines the walls watching.

steps.position: Instructor introduces Suzy Q. Students in line — woman in black shorts shows cross-in-front position. Foot clearly crossing in front of standing foot, not behind. Instructor calls 'little circular, just a circle.' Conga drums visible in background.
steps.instruction: Instructor introduces Suzy Q. Students in line — woman in black shorts shows cross-in-front position. Foot clearly crossing in front of standing foot, not behind. Instructor calls 'little circular, just a circle.' Conga drums visible in background.
steps.instructor_tip: little circular, just a circle, full circle

steps.position: Students attempt circular Suzy Q. The line has begun rotating — dancers are turning to face different directions (the four walls). Instructor calls 'around the world.' Woman in black shorts shows the cross position mid-rotation. Man in pink shirt follows.
steps.instruction: Students attempt circular Suzy Q. The line has begun rotating — dancers are turning to face different directions (the four walls). Instructor calls 'around the world.' Woman in black shorts shows the cross position mid-rotation. Man in pink shirt follows.
steps.instructor_tip: around the world. We go and 12, 9, 6, basic and 1, 2, 3

steps.position: Circular Suzy Q continues. Students have rotated approximately 90 degrees from starting position. The line is staggered — instructor has called 'small steps.' Woman in black shorts is mid-cross, leg picked up. Man in pink shirt mirrors.
steps.instruction: Circular Suzy Q continues. Students have rotated approximately 90 degrees from starting position. The line is staggered — instructor has called 'small steps.' Woman in black shorts is mid-cross, leg picked up. Man in pink shirt mirrors.
steps.instructor_tip: circular and 1, 2, 3, this is for basic and 1, 2, around the world

steps.position: FOG MACHINE ACTIVATES. Visibility drops significantly. Students continue moving — the combo sequence begins. Instructor calls 'combo and card out.' The woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt are the primary visible dancers. Basic step resumes as the combo starting point.
steps.instruction: FOG MACHINE ACTIVATES. Visibility drops significantly. Students continue moving — the combo sequence begins. Instructor calls 'combo and card out.' The woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt are the primary visible dancers. Basic step resumes as the combo starting point.
steps.instructor_tip: Now we go combo and card out and 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7

steps.position: Full speed Suzy Q in heavy fog. Woman in black shorts shows the cross position clearly — foot in front, leg picked up after the cross. Man in pink shirt is in the step position of the cross-step-cross pattern. Both dancers show good 'always in front' technique.
steps.instruction: Full speed Suzy Q in heavy fog. Woman in black shorts shows the cross position clearly — foot in front, leg picked up after the cross. Man in pink shirt is in the step position of the cross-step-cross pattern. Both dancers show good 'always in front' technique.

steps.position: Suzy Q at speed — both primary dancers show the cross-step-cross pattern simultaneously. The woman's foot is clearly crossing in front. Man in pink shirt mirrors. The fog creates atmospheric effect but footwork is still visible.
steps.instruction: Suzy Q at speed — both primary dancers show the cross-step-cross pattern simultaneously. The woman's foot is clearly crossing in front. Man in pink shirt mirrors. The fog creates atmospheric effect but footwork is still visible.

steps.position: Students in basic step — the anchor count (7) is visible in the planted foot position of the woman in black shorts. Weight shifted but foot not moved. Man in pink shirt shows the same anchor. This is the 'keep your weight planted' moment.
steps.instruction: Students in basic step — the anchor count (7) is visible in the planted foot position of the woman in black shorts. Weight shifted but foot not moved. Man in pink shirt shows the same anchor. This is the 'keep your weight planted' moment.

steps.position: Forward travel on counts 1-2. Woman in black shorts steps forward, man in pink shirt steps forward. Both show small steps — no large lunges. The fog is thick but the footwork pattern is clear from the leg positions.
steps.instruction: Forward travel on counts 1-2. Woman in black shorts steps forward, man in pink shirt steps forward. Both show small steps — no large lunges. The fog is thick but the footwork pattern is clear from the leg positions.

steps.position: Back travel on counts 5-6. The line of dancers steps back together. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt show the backward travel. Fog is at maximum density — dancers are silhouettes but movement is clear.
steps.instruction: Back travel on counts 5-6. The line of dancers steps back together. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt show the backward travel. Fog is at maximum density — dancers are silhouettes but movement is clear.
steps.instructor_tip: 6, 7. OK. Can we hold it? 1 more time. 1 right turn.

steps.position: Suzy Q cross position — woman in black shorts shows the cross-in-front clearly. Man in pink shirt is in the step position. The pattern 'cross, step, cross' is visible across the two dancers' positions.
steps.instruction: Suzy Q cross position — woman in black shorts shows the cross-in-front clearly. Man in pink shirt is in the step position. The pattern 'cross, step, cross' is visible across the two dancers' positions.

steps.position: The 'step' in cross-step-cross — woman in black shorts has her foot out to the side (the step between the two crosses). Man in pink shirt is in the cross position. The alternating pattern between the two dancers shows the timing offset.
steps.instruction: The 'step' in cross-step-cross — woman in black shorts has her foot out to the side (the step between the two crosses). Man in pink shirt is in the cross position. The alternating pattern between the two dancers shows the timing offset.

steps.position: Basic step forward travel. The line of dancers moves forward together. Woman in black shorts leads the line, man in pink shirt follows. Small steps visible — no bouncing in the upper body.
steps.instruction: Basic step forward travel. The line of dancers moves forward together. Woman in black shorts leads the line, man in pink shirt follows. Small steps visible — no bouncing in the upper body.

steps.position: Basic step back travel. Dancers step back on counts 5-6. The fog has lightened slightly — footwork more visible. Woman in black shorts shows the back step with weight fully transferred.
steps.instruction: Basic step back travel. Dancers step back on counts 5-6. The fog has lightened slightly — footwork more visible. Woman in black shorts shows the back step with weight fully transferred.

steps.position: Suzy Q cross position — the cross-in-front technique is clearly visible. Woman in black shorts has her crossing foot clearly in front of the standing foot. This is the key teaching moment: 'always in front, never behind.'
steps.instruction: Suzy Q cross position — the cross-in-front technique is clearly visible. Woman in black shorts has her crossing foot clearly in front of the standing foot. This is the key teaching moment: 'always in front, never behind.'

steps.position: After the cross — woman in black shorts shows the leg pickup position. The foot is lifted off the floor after the cross, preparing for the next step. This is the 'pick up your leg after the cross — don't drag your foot' teaching point.
steps.instruction: After the cross — woman in black shorts shows the leg pickup position. The foot is lifted off the floor after the cross, preparing for the next step. This is the 'pick up your leg after the cross — don't drag your foot' teaching point.
steps.instructor_tip: Give it up for the ladies!

steps.position: The combo sequence begins — 'card out' position. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt show the card-out arm position. This is the transition from basic step into the combo that leads to the inside turn.
steps.instruction: The combo sequence begins — 'card out' position. Woman in black shorts and man in pink shirt show the card-out arm position. This is the transition from basic step into the combo that leads to the inside turn.

steps.position: The 'around' portion of the combo — woman in black shorts is moving around the man in pink shirt. This is the 'around the world' element within the combo sequence. Both dancers show the spatial relationship of the around movement.
steps.instruction: The 'around' portion of the combo — woman in black shorts is moving around the man in pink shirt. This is the 'around the world' element within the combo sequence. Both dancers show the spatial relationship of the around movement.

steps.position: The anchor position within the combo — woman in black shorts plants her foot on count 7. Man in pink shirt shows the anchor on his side. This is the 'anchor the 7' teaching point applied within the combo context.
steps.instruction: The anchor position within the combo — woman in black shorts plants her foot on count 7. Man in pink shirt shows the anchor on his side. This is the 'anchor the 7' teaching point applied within the combo context.

steps.position: Inside turn setup — man in pink shirt raises his arm on count 1 to signal the turn. Woman in black shorts is preparing to turn to her right. The arm is LOW — demonstrating 'don't reach high, keep your arm low.'
steps.instruction: Inside turn setup — man in pink shirt raises his arm on count 1 to signal the turn. Woman in black shorts is preparing to turn to her right. The arm is LOW — demonstrating 'don't reach high, keep your arm low.'

steps.position: Follower (woman in black shorts) begins turning to her right on count 6. Leader (man in pink shirt) guides with elbow activation. The turn is just beginning — 'start turning on count 6, not before.'
steps.instruction: Follower (woman in black shorts) begins turning to her right on count 6. Leader (man in pink shirt) guides with elbow activation. The turn is just beginning — 'start turning on count 6, not before.'

steps.position: Mid-turn position — follower is rotating to her right, leader maintains the right-to-right connection. The leader's arm is up but not high — elbow is the activation point. The follower's momentum carries the turn.
steps.instruction: Mid-turn position — follower is rotating to her right, leader maintains the right-to-right connection. The leader's arm is up but not high — elbow is the activation point. The follower's momentum carries the turn.

steps.position: Turn nearing completion — follower has rotated approximately 270 degrees. Leader's arm is coming down. The 'keep your 7 away from your partner' principle is visible — there is space between the dancers, not crowding.
steps.instruction: Turn nearing completion — follower has rotated approximately 270 degrees. Leader's arm is coming down. The 'keep your 7 away from your partner' principle is visible — there is space between the dancers, not crowding.

steps.position: The count-8 landing — follower plants her foot and absorbs the weight. This is the deliberate pause before continuing with 1-2-3. Leader is in position, right-to-right connection maintained. 'Land on count 8 — don't rush the landing.'
steps.instruction: The count-8 landing — follower plants her foot and absorbs the weight. This is the deliberate pause before continuing with 1-2-3. Leader is in position, right-to-right connection maintained. 'Land on count 8 — don't rush the landing.'

steps.position: Transition complete — both dancers resume basic step on count 1 after the count-8 landing. Right-to-right hand hold maintained. The flow from inside turn back to basic is smooth — 'connection and simplicity.'
steps.instruction: Transition complete — both dancers resume basic step on count 1 after the count-8 landing. Right-to-right hand hold maintained. The flow from inside turn back to basic is smooth — 'connection and simplicity.'

video_breakdown.description: BASIC STEP (solo, slow) -> BASIC STEP (around the world, solo) -> INSIDE TURN (solo demo) -> PARTNER WORK: BASIC + INSIDE TURN -> TRANSITION TO CROSS BODY

steps.position: Instructor stands facing the mirror, feet hip-width apart, weight centered, arms relaxed at sides. Cap on backwards, neon shoes visible. Students line the back wall watching.
steps.instruction: Instructor stands facing the mirror, feet hip-width apart, weight centered, arms relaxed at sides. Cap on backwards, neon shoes visible. Students line the back wall watching.

steps.position: Instructor steps forward, weight fully on front foot, slight hip drop. Body remains upright. Arms swing naturally with the step. Circular arc begins.
steps.instruction: Instructor steps forward, weight fully on front foot, slight hip drop. Body remains upright. Arms swing naturally with the step. Circular arc begins.

steps.position: Instructor steps back, weight transfers to back foot. Hip drops on count 6. Feet show clear directional change — beginning the 'around the world' arc toward 9 o'clock.
steps.instruction: Instructor steps back, weight transfers to back foot. Hip drops on count 6. Feet show clear directional change — beginning the 'around the world' arc toward 9 o'clock.

steps.position: Instructor faces slightly left of mirror, demonstrating the directional shift of the circular basic. Knee visible on the stepping side. Body upright. Mouth open — counting aloud.
steps.instruction: Instructor faces slightly left of mirror, demonstrating the directional shift of the circular basic. Knee visible on the stepping side. Body upright. Mouth open — counting aloud.

steps.position: Instructor has rotated body to face a new angle. Back step clearly visible with neon shoe lifted. Weight shifting. The 'around the world' rotation is in progress.
steps.instruction: Instructor has rotated body to face a new angle. Back step clearly visible with neon shoe lifted. Weight shifting. The 'around the world' rotation is in progress.

steps.position: Instructor faces slightly right, weight anchored on standing foot, opposite knee bent. Arms extended slightly for balance. This is the 'hold it' anchor position between directional changes.
steps.instruction: Instructor faces slightly right, weight anchored on standing foot, opposite knee bent. Arms extended slightly for balance. This is the 'hold it' anchor position between directional changes.

steps.position: Instructor demonstrates knee lift on the stepping side — 'knee on this side now.' Body stays upright. Neon shoes show one foot grounded, one lifted. Mouth open counting.
steps.instruction: Instructor demonstrates knee lift on the stepping side — 'knee on this side now.' Body stays upright. Neon shoes show one foot grounded, one lifted. Mouth open counting.
steps.instructor_tip: Cross body, knee on this side now, I go, I stay upright

steps.position: Instructor collects weight to center, feet nearly together, body upright. This is the reset between 'around the world' repetitions. Clean, balanced, ready to redirect.
steps.instruction: Instructor collects weight to center, feet nearly together, body upright. This is the reset between 'around the world' repetitions. Clean, balanced, ready to redirect.

steps.position: Instructor has rotated to face away from mirror (6 o'clock position). Back to camera shows 'COOL PEOPLE PARTY AT 11AM' shirt. Foot lifted mid-step. Completing the full circle.
steps.instruction: Instructor has rotated to face away from mirror (6 o'clock position). Back to camera shows 'COOL PEOPLE PARTY AT 11AM' shirt. Foot lifted mid-step. Completing the full circle.

steps.position: Instructor stands with feet parallel, weight anchored evenly. Facing mirror again — full 360° circle completed. Students in mirror reflection watching closely.
steps.instruction: Instructor stands with feet parallel, weight anchored evenly. Facing mirror again — full 360° circle completed. Students in mirror reflection watching closely.
steps.instructor_tip: Say, get ready, here it comes!

steps.position: Instructor begins another circular basic, stepping to a new angle. Body upright, arms relaxed. Demonstrating the continuous 'around the world' pattern.
steps.instruction: Instructor begins another circular basic, stepping to a new angle. Body upright, arms relaxed. Demonstrating the continuous 'around the world' pattern.

steps.position: Instructor pivots to new clock position. Neon shoes show foot placement mid-arc. Weight transferring. The circular pattern continues through all angles.
steps.instruction: Instructor pivots to new clock position. Neon shoes show foot placement mid-arc. Weight transferring. The circular pattern continues through all angles.

steps.position: Instructor continues the circular basic, now facing a different wall. Feet show clear step pattern. Body remains upright throughout the rotation.
steps.instruction: Instructor continues the circular basic, now facing a different wall. Feet show clear step pattern. Body remains upright throughout the rotation.

steps.position: Instructor turns to face the room (no longer facing mirror). Arm begins to extend outward — setting up the inside turn demonstration. Students visible watching from sides.
steps.instruction: Instructor turns to face the room (no longer facing mirror). Arm begins to extend outward — setting up the inside turn demonstration. Students visible watching from sides.

steps.position: Instructor's right arm extends fully to the side, demonstrating the turn lead arc. Body faces room. Mouth open explaining. This is the 'raise the arm' teaching moment.
steps.instruction: Instructor's right arm extends fully to the side, demonstrating the turn lead arc. Body faces room. Mouth open explaining. This is the 'raise the arm' teaching moment.
steps.instructor_tip: Execute the right turn with clean, controlled rotation

steps.position: Instructor faces room fully, both arms extended in a wide open position — demonstrating the frame and connection point for the inside turn. Students on both sides watching. Level 3 syllabus visible above.
steps.instruction: Instructor faces room fully, both arms extended in a wide open position — demonstrating the frame and connection point for the inside turn. Students on both sides watching. Level 3 syllabus visible above.

steps.position: Instructor (white shirt, neon shoes) faces female partner (orange top, black shorts, latin heels). Both smiling, stepping in sync. Open hold established — hands joined, arms relaxed.
steps.instruction: Instructor (white shirt, neon shoes) faces female partner (orange top, black shorts, latin heels). Both smiling, stepping in sync. Open hold established — hands joined, arms relaxed.

steps.position: Both partners step together in basic. Instructor's back to camera shows 'COOL PEOPLE PARTY AT 11AM.' Partner smiling, weight on front foot. Hands joined at waist height.
steps.instruction: Both partners step together in basic. Instructor's back to camera shows 'COOL PEOPLE PARTY AT 11AM.' Partner smiling, weight on front foot. Hands joined at waist height.
steps.instructor_tip: All right, Lily, you got it, now transition, you ready?

steps.position: Both partners step back simultaneously. Partner's heel visible lifting in latin heels. Instructor's neon shoe steps back. Connection maintained through joined hands. Smiling — good energy.
steps.instruction: Both partners step back simultaneously. Partner's heel visible lifting in latin heels. Instructor's neon shoe steps back. Connection maintained through joined hands. Smiling — good energy.

steps.position: Instructor begins raising joined right hand to create the arch. Partner's weight shifts as she prepares to step under. Both bodies upright. The turn lead begins on count 5.
steps.instruction: Instructor begins raising joined right hand to create the arch. Partner's weight shifts as she prepares to step under. Both bodies upright. The turn lead begins on count 5.

steps.position: Partner is mid-rotation clockwise under the arch. Instructor's arm is raised overhead guiding. Partner's body has turned approximately 180°. Both maintaining frame.
steps.instruction: Partner is mid-rotation clockwise under the arch. Instructor's arm is raised overhead guiding. Partner's body has turned approximately 180°. Both maintaining frame.

steps.position: Partner nearly faces instructor again — rotation almost complete. Instructor's arm begins to lower. Connection about to be re-established. Partner's feet landing cleanly.
steps.instruction: Partner nearly faces instructor again — rotation almost complete. Instructor's arm begins to lower. Connection about to be re-established. Partner's feet landing cleanly.

steps.position: Partner faces instructor, turn complete. Both stepping in basic. Partner laughing — successful turn. Instructor smiling. Open hold re-established at waist height.
steps.instruction: Partner faces instructor, turn complete. Both stepping in basic. Partner laughing — successful turn. Instructor smiling. Open hold re-established at waist height.

steps.position: Both partners in basic step, facing each other. Instructor's back to camera. Partner smiling. Weight anchored. This is the reset between turn repetitions.
steps.instruction: Both partners in basic step, facing each other. Instructor's back to camera. Partner smiling. Weight anchored. This is the reset between turn repetitions.

steps.position: Instructor raises arm again for a second inside turn. Partner's arm follows upward. Both bodies upright. The repeated turn sequence demonstrates the 'get ready, here it comes' cue.
steps.instruction: Instructor raises arm again for a second inside turn. Partner's arm follows upward. Both bodies upright. The repeated turn sequence demonstrates the 'get ready, here it comes' cue.

steps.position: Partner rotating clockwise again. Instructor's arm fully extended overhead. Clear view of the turn arch from the side. Partner's body compact during rotation.
steps.instruction: Partner rotating clockwise again. Instructor's arm fully extended overhead. Clear view of the turn arch from the side. Partner's body compact during rotation.

steps.position: Instructor faces room, arms extended to re-catch partner. Partner completing rotation. Both stepping. The landing on count 1 is visible — weight transferring to new position.
steps.instruction: Instructor faces room, arms extended to re-catch partner. Partner completing rotation. Both stepping. The landing on count 1 is visible — weight transferring to new position.

steps.position: Instructor and partner in a transitional position — instructor's arm raised high, partner stepping through. This is the cross body lead entry. Instructor's body opens to the side.
steps.instruction: Instructor and partner in a transitional position — instructor's arm raised high, partner stepping through. This is the cross body lead entry. Instructor's body opens to the side.

steps.position: Partner's hand on instructor's back, instructor's hand on partner's back — closed/cross body position. Both stepping forward. Partner passing across instructor's body line.
steps.instruction: Partner's hand on instructor's back, instructor's hand on partner's back — closed/cross body position. Both stepping forward. Partner passing across instructor's body line.
steps.instructor_tip: Cross body, knee on this side now

steps.position: Both partners in open hold, stepping in basic. Partner on instructor's left side. Hands joined. Smiling. Demonstrating the reset position after cross body lead.
steps.instruction: Both partners in open hold, stepping in basic. Partner on instructor's left side. Hands joined. Smiling. Demonstrating the reset position after cross body lead.

steps.position: Both partners in open hold, instructor's back to camera showing full shirt text. Partner facing camera smiling. Clean hand connection visible. Weight anchored on back step.
steps.instruction: Both partners in open hold, instructor's back to camera showing full shirt text. Partner facing camera smiling. Clean hand connection visible. Weight anchored on back step.
